overall: Violation found: the Board entered executive session on Feb 7, 2012 to discuss a non-permitted alcohol policy topic. Prior open-session re-vote and minutes release cured it, but the AG ordered a review of the minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board entered executive session on Feb 7, 2012 for an improper purpose, because it discussed a town alcohol policy amendment in session.
allegations.key_passage: The alcohol policy discussion was not appropriate under any of the Open Meeting Law's ten enumerated purposes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board took improper action during the Feb 7, 2012 executive session, where it voted to amend the alcohol policy by roll call.
allegations.key_passage: We find that these actions were appropriate to remedy the violation, and order no additional relief.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to hold a public hearing on the amendment to the town's alcohol policy.
allegations.key_passage: Because this determination concerns only compliance with the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review whether Massachusetts General Law and/or the Alcoholic Beverages Control Commission (ABCC) required the Board to hold a public hearing prior to adopting a municipal alcohol policy.

remedy: Review the minutes of the February 7, 2012 executive session and release all portions that were not appropriate for discussion in executive session, unless the attorney/client privilege or a Public Records Law exemption applies.
For the portions appropriate for executive session, determine whether continued nondisclosure is warranted and publicly announce that determination during an open session meeting.
Complete both parts of the review within thirty days of receiving the determination and certify to the Attorney General by letter that the Board has complied.
remedy_passage: Both aspects of this review must occur within thirty (30) days of receiving this determination, and the Board shall certify to this office by letter that it has complied with our order.
